Vicinity
The project site is located in Erie, Colorado, draining ultimately to the Rural Canal.

title: A 233-acre parcel on Erie’s eastern edge
text:
Existing conditions
Pre-development land cover is predominantly agricultural with scattered residential parcels. NRCS soils data classifies the area as Hydrologic Soil Group C.

title: A 233-acre parcel on Erie’s eastern edge
text:
Proposed development
The post-development condition assumes mixed-use residential at typical Erie densities.

title: A 233-acre parcel on Erie’s eastern edge
text:
Design constraints

Key constraint The Rural Canal outfall limits the allowable release rate to historic 2-year peak flow.

title: From station record to design depths
text:
02 · Precipitation


GEV fit on 71 years of GHCN-D data, cross-validated against NOAA Atlas 14.

title: From station record to design depths
text:
Annual maximum series
The annual maximum 24-hour precipitation depth was extracted from the Boulder GHCN-D record (1953–2024). After screening for missing data, 71 complete water years remained for frequency analysis.

title: From station record to design depths
text:
GEV fit
The Generalized Extreme Value distribution was fit using L-moments via the lmomco package.

title: About this project
text:
Project
This site documents the final project for CIVE 573 (Urban Stormwater) — an undeveloped 233-acre parcel on the eastern edge of Erie, Colorado.
The R workflow — data tidying, GEV fitting, hyetograph generation, and result visualization — doubles as the final project for ESS 580.

title: A 233-acre stormwater design for Erie, Colorado.
text:
Walk through the project
This site documents the urban stormwater design for an undeveloped 233-acre parcel on the eastern edge of Erie, Colorado. The work pairs a hydrologic frequency analysis built in R with a SWMM model of the developed condition to size a constructed wetland park for full-spectrum detention.

Site — vicinity, land use, soils, constraints
Precipitation — GEV fit, NOAA Atlas 14 comparison
Design storms — 2- through 100-yr hyetographs
Hydrographs — CUHP and SWMM routing
Results — peak reductions, WQCV, TSS load
About — course, stack, references
